My land is 4.1 mu total. Wheat goes in first, then after I harvest it in June, maize goes into the same ground. That's how I've done it for fifty years, same as my mother before me. The land doesn't rest, but neither do I.

**Wheat (October through June):**
I'll plant wheat in October when the soil temperature feels right — I can tell by how the ground feels underfoot. I'll buy improved seed from the township supply shop, same as last few years. The county station handed out leaflets about new varieties but I can't read them, so I ask my son what the neighbors are using. For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer plus some urea — and then topdress urea again at jointing in spring. I know I should water at least three times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once at heading. My well reaches water, so I'm not worried. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and one round for powdery mildew near heading. I'll rotary till after the maize stalks are chopped up.

**Maize (June through September/October):**
Right after wheat harvest I plant maize the same day or next. No time to plow — I go straight in. I use Zhengdan 958, everyone in the village does. I put fertilizer down at planting and topdress when the maize is knee-high. Summer rains usually help but I'll pump water once or twice if it looks dry. I'll spray for weeds early and watch for corn borer in August.

My children help during harvest. Otherwise I manage myself.
